errors.text_span: appearing to be ordered by decreasing size
errors.evidence: The slices are not ordered by decreasing size. The chart groups slices under three inner categories (Contradiction Resolution, Context Tracking, Context Retrieving), and the arrangement follows that grouping, not a size ordering.
Privacy Protection is colored dark red in the figure, not light red. Light red corresponds to Prioritization.
Prioritization is colored light red/salmon, not pink. The reference describes it as 'light red'.
Dynamic Environment is colored dark blue in the figure, not teal. Teal colors correspond to the Context Retrieving category.
Multitasking is colored dark teal, not simply 'green'. The reference describes it as 'dark teal'.

errors.text_span: The chart consists of nine slices
errors.evidence: The chart has a two-ring structure: an inner ring with three slices (Contradiction Resolution, Context Tracking, Context Retrieving) and an outer ring with nine slices. The description treats the inner categories inconsistently.

errors.text_span: A legend labels each slice with its corresponding capability and sample count.
errors.evidence: There is no legend in the figure. The reference explicitly states 'No legend is given.' Labels are placed outside the slices with lines pointing to them.

The description fails to mention the inner ring structure with three central categories (Contradiction Resolution, Context Tracking, Context Retrieving) that group the outer slices. This dual-ring organization is a key structural feature of the chart.
The description does not mention that Triggering (100, light blue) is one of the outer slices. It is visible in the figure and listed in the reference.
Contradiction Resolution is shown as a brown/dark red inner segment in the chart, not white with blue text. The text inside it is white.

errors.text_span: A central gray circle appears within the pie chart
errors.evidence: The central circle appears white, not gray, based on the figure.

Personalization appears to be a medium/salmon red in the figure (between Prioritization's light red and Privacy Protection's dark red). The reference describes Personalization as 'red', which is acceptable, but the description also labels Prioritization as pink and Privacy Protection as light red—creating an inconsistent color mapping.

Memorization is described as light teal and Dynamic Instruction as teal in the reference, though both are in the teal family. Grouping them together as a single entry makes the description ambiguous about their distinct segments.
